prompt: Write a note to a friend about impressions from a trip abroad. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Dear friend,

I have been home for a week now, and I still think about the trip every day. I want to tell you what stayed with me, because I think you would enjoy hearing it.

The first thing I noticed was how slowly people eat. A meal in Lisbon is not something you finish in twenty minutes. You sit, you talk, and nobody looks at a clock.

I found this hard at first. I kept waiting for the bill. By the third day I had stopped waiting, and I enjoyed my food more than I have in years.

The streets were another surprise. They are narrow and steep, and you cannot hurry up them. I walked about ten miles a day, and my legs hurt, but I saw more than any bus would have shown me.

People were kind to me, even though I knew only a few words of their language. A woman at a bakery taught me how to ask for bread. She laughed at my first try, then made me say it again until I got it right.

I think about that often. She did not have to help me. She did it because she wanted me to do well, and that is a good way to treat a stranger.

I also learned something about myself. I had planned every hour of the trip before I left, and by the second day the plan was useless. The best moments came when I had nothing planned at all.

One evening I sat by the river and watched the light change on the water. I had no place to be. I do not remember the last time I could say that.

I came home with a few small gifts, some bad photographs, and a better sense of how much I do not know. I count that last part as the most useful thing I brought back.

I would like you to go there yourself. You do not need much money or much time. You only need to be willing to walk slowly and to let yourself be a beginner again.

When you have a free evening, come over and I will show you the photographs. I will cook something from the trip, and I promise to make it last longer than twenty minutes.

Write and tell me how you have been. I want to hear about your work, your family, and anything new you have learned lately.

Samuel
